clue.text: Word is we cavort with King George when his wife's away

definitions.note: describes the man rather than naming him

parts.note: Georgius Rex, the royal cipher of a King George

indicators.note: to cavort is to caper about wildly, so the letters of the preceding words leap into a new order

parts.note: as in 'as he left' meaning 'when he left'
the letters of these three words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that the royal household frolics with the king whenever the queen is out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: GR + AS goes first, then the jumbled WORD IS WE ends the answer as SWIDOWER, giving GRASS WIDOWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass widower is a married man temporarily left alone because his spouse is away travelling or on holiday.

clue.text: Excellent machinist originally brought in to let out garments

indicators.note: things brought in to a place end up inside it, so these letters go into the middle of the next word

parts.note: to let out a property is to rent it
A1, first-rate, written with an I for the 1

indicators.note: originally points to the very beginning of the word it follows, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of machinist

explanation.surface: A top-class machine operator is hired in to let out some clothes that have become too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' looks like tailoring, matching the garments, but it means letting a property for money. A1 for excellent is written with an I.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old-fashioned or literary word for clothing, the things a person wears.

clue.text: Part of guitar made from solid wood

parts.note: a sound structure is solid and firm
box is a hard timber from the box tree

explanation.surface: A section of a guitar is crafted out of solid timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The soundbox is the hollow body of a guitar or violin that resonates and amplifies the strings' vibrations.

clue.text: Went west upriver

parts.note: the compass abbreviation

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the river's name from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another on the England-Wales border

explanation.surface: Someone travelled westward, heading upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went' reads as travelling, but it is the euphemism 'went to the toilet', the past tense of wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Weed is the past tense of wee, to urinate, and 'went' is a common polite euphemism for that act.

clue.text: Type of spanner?

parts.note: surface reading: a kind of wrench from the toolbox
setter's reading: something that spans a gap, here a moat, and can be hauled up

explanation.walkthrough: A spanner in the toolbox sense is a wrench; read literally, it is anything that spans, and this bridge can be raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawbridge is a hinged bridge across a castle moat that is pulled up, so it is a kind of span.

clue.text: Most unpleasant in defeat

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a verb, to get the better of someone

explanation.surface: The nastiest thing about losing.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bad describes the most unpleasant; as a verb it means to beat an opponent in a contest.

clue.text: Organ repaired at last after the woman returned and tried again

indicators.note: something that has returned has gone back the way it came, so the pronoun is read backwards

parts.note: the pronoun for a woman
the organ of hearing

indicators.note: at last means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of repaired

explanation.surface: An organ was mended in the end once she came back and had another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks musical, sitting beside 'repaired', but it is the one you hear with.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that is reheard is tried again in court, given a second hearing before a judge.

clue.text: Maybe Pew's getting fit for game

parts.note: Blind Pew is the sightless pirate in Treasure Island, so he is an example of a blind man
buff means physically fit and muscular

explanation.surface: Perhaps a church bench is being made suitable for a sporting contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Pew looks like a church seat, but it is Blind Pew from Treasure Island; 'maybe' flags him as one example of a blind man.
explanation.definitionFit: Blind man's buff is a children's party game where a blindfolded player tries to catch the others.

clue.text: Good to put on oldish pants transformed by thorough cleaning

indicators.note: something transformed has changed its form, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: pi, short for pious, is crosswordese for good
the letters of these words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fit to wear on a pair of tired old trousers after a really good clean.
explanation.walkthrough: PI is added to OLDISH PANTS, and all thirteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit and polish is the scrupulous cleaning and shining associated with military boot care, hence any meticulous clean.

clue.text: Convenient opportunity to make left turn that's safe

parts.note: the standard abbreviation

indicators.note: to turn round is to face the other way, so the abbreviation that follows is read backwards

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
a sure bet is a safe one

explanation.surface: Road-safety advice: wait for the right moment before turning left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left turn' reads as a driving manoeuvre, but turn only reverses i.e., the abbreviation for 'that is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at your leisure means when it suits you, at a time of convenience.

clue.text: Look in to collect small flier

indicators.note: to collect something is to take it in, so the joined words gather a letter between them

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance, as in an air of mystery
in fashion, trendy
the clothing-size abbreviation

explanation.surface: Pop in to pick up a little pamphlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a leaflet you might collect; it is something that flies.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a lighter-than-air powered aircraft, so it is a craft that flies through the sky.

clue.text: Very much against overturning result

indicators.note: overturning flips a thing upside down, so the short word for against is read backwards

parts.note: as in 'have something on someone', held against them
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: Strongly opposed to reversing an election outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'no end' means enormously, as in 'it pleased him no end'.

clue.text: Remove unruly brats in turn

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly and out of control, so the letters of the children are scrambled

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: Take away badly behaved children one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In turn' looks like 'one after another', but turn is the stage act placed after the jumbled BRATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract something is to take it out or extract it, a formal verb for removing.

clue.text: Poem, circa the end of 1640, revised by Milton perhaps

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so all these letters are rearranged

parts.note: letters for the anagram
letters for the anagram

indicators.note: the end of the number is its final character, a zero read as a letter

parts.note: the final digit 0 is read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A poem from around 1640, edited by Milton himself perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The date and the poet make one think of Paradise Lost, but Milton here is Spontini's 1804 one-act opéra comique about the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Spontini's Milton is a light opera with spoken dialogue, so it is an example of the genre.

clue.text: Development of prime lots around old capital

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the abbreviation for old
a development reshapes land or a plan, so these letters are built into a new order

parts.note: letters to be rearranged
the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Building on choice plots of land around the former seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A metropolis is a country's chief city, often its seat of government, so a capital is the classic example.

clue.text: Taken from Ganymede napping in garden

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted straight out of the words that follow

parts.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: Seized from the cupbearer of the gods while he dozed in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Ganymede was the beautiful youth Zeus carried off to be cupbearer, which fits 'taken'; the answer sits across his name and the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden is the biblical paradise, the garden where Adam and Eve lived.

clue.text: Affects to be in film after priest objects

indicators.note: after says the pieces named before it come later, so the cleric's abbreviation goes ahead of the film

parts.note: Pr is an abbreviation for priest
E.T. is Spielberg's 1982 film
ends are aims or objectives

explanation.surface: An actor puts on airs to appear in a movie after a cleric protests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objects' reads as a verb, protests, but it is a noun meaning goals.
explanation.definitionFit: To affect a manner is to put it on falsely, which is to feign or make believe.

clue.text: Steals darts

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pinches or nicks something
second meaning: moves quickly, as in nipping out to the shop

explanation.surface: A thief lifts the darts from a pub board.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip is informal British for both stealing something and moving quickly somewhere.

clue.text: Artist's photo to fool Oberleutnant at first

parts.note: short for picture
an ass is a foolish person

indicators.note: at first points to the start of the word, so only its opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of Oberleutnant

explanation.surface: A painter's photograph is meant to deceive a German officer, a wartime ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like a verb, to deceive, but it is the noun ass.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, among the most famous artists of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Photo of Spice Girl getting something to eat

parts.note: Ginger Spice, Geri Halliwell's name in the pop group the Spice Girls; ginger is also a spice
a snap is a snapshot

explanation.surface: A tabloid shot of a pop star caught having a bite to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Photo of' Ginger reverses the order: the subject comes first, then the snap.
explanation.definitionFit: A gingersnap is a crisp biscuit flavoured with ginger, which is food you might munch.

clue.text: Great number on board

parts.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
board is an old word for a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A large figure written on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable describes someone eminent or remarkable, as in a great figure worth noting.

clue.text: Ammunition recently stolen by young men

parts.note: a buck is a dashing young man
hot goods are freshly stolen

explanation.surface: Weapons and rounds that some lads have just nicked.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay comes in reverse clue order: the young men first, then the stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckshot is coarse lead pellets fired from a shotgun, a kind of ammunition for hunting deer.

clue.text: Pickled meat or duck?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pork trimmings preserved in brine
second meaning: a verb, to plunge into water

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes it look like a choice of dishes, cured pork or roast duck, but duck is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Souse is meat steeped in brine or vinegar, and to souse someone is to drench or dunk them.

clue.text: Including all fifty books wrapped by volunteers earlier

indicators.note: something wrapped by another is enclosed inside it, so the testament abbreviation sits within the volunteers

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve force
the Old Testament, a group of books of the Bible
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Counting every one of fifty volumes that the volunteers had packaged up before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earlier' places the wrapped unit TOTA before the fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: A total figure is an aggregate that counts everything, leaving nothing out.

clue.text: Loathsome Foreign Office bully oddly ignored

parts.note: the abbreviation for the British Foreign Office

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions leaves only the second and fourth letters

parts.note: the even letters of bully

explanation.surface: A hateful government department pushes others around, oddly overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul describes something disgusting or detestable, such as a vile smell or deed.

clue.text: Is inevitable after fellow discovers crack

indicators.note: after places what precedes it behind what follows, so the fellow's abbreviation leads the answer

parts.note: the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written
something sure is certain to happen

explanation.surface: Fate dictates that a colleague will find a weakness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a long narrow opening or split, such as one in rock or ice.

clue.text: Award by university occupying writers of many different things

parts.note: the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: a letter occupying something takes up a place inside it

parts.note: nibs are pen points
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A university prize goes to authors of all sorts of material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' suggests authors, but they are pen nibs, and U sits inside before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus volume or bill gathers several varied items together into one collection.

clue.text: Head of Obstetrics happens to employ a variety of large visual aids

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Obstetrics

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so the verb holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: as in 'it came to pass', to happen

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters of the size word are rearranged

parts.note: letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A senior hospital doctor turns out to use a big range of eye-test equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happens' is the verb 'passes', as in 'it came to pass'; 'large' is not a size here but letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera glasses are small binoculars for watching a stage performance, so they help one see.
